subject: PO preauth & split-invoice flow — pricing lanes and netterm compromise

Cc: procurements@healthline.com
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Procurement requirements: PO format, pre-auth window, and split invoices

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the call today. A quick follow-up with the procurement constraints we need Redwood to support before we can push this to our finance team: 

- Blanket PO accepted, but must include: entity_code, PO_owner, legal_entity_number in the header.
- Invoice cadence: ability to issue partial invoices (split by milestone) + a monthly consolidated statement for reconciliation.
- Net terms: standard is net60, but we can consider net30 for prepaid credits.
- Pre-authorization: for any early invoices (outside standard cadence) we need vendor to provide a preauth reference and a PO-ack window of 5 business days.
- Minimum invoice amount: Finance requires invoices >= $1,000 unless pre-approved.

I've attached our PO template (Healthline_PO_template_v2.pdf) and a high-level checklist. Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) accept the header fields as-is, (b) support split invoices plus consolidated monthly statement, and (c) offer a pricing option that preserves a discount if we prepay a portion upfront?

If helpful, Adam Green (copied on procurements) is our AP contact for ERP mapping. We are hoping to close commercial terms next week.

Best,
Monica Li
Head of Procurement — Healthline Labs
monica.li@healthline.com

--
Healthline Labs | Procurement

Subject: Re: Procurement requirements: PO format, pre-auth window, and split invoices

Monica — thanks for the clear list and the template. Short answers up front: yes, we can support the header fields and split invoicing; we have a couple of standard patterns for the preauth/early-invoice flow.

Options to consider (high-level):
1) Prepaid credit lane + monthly settlement: customer prepays an agreed credit amount (3-month minimum), we invoice against that credit for milestone deliveries; we still produce a monthly consolidated statement for your ERP. This preserves a prepaid discount.
2) Net-term split: upfront partial payment (30% on contract sign), remainder on net60 with split invoices for milestones — discount tiers apply based on committed ARR.
3) Fully invoiced monthly with PO-ack gating: we will only accept early invoices with an attached preauth reference and our system can enforce a 5-business-day PO-ack window before an invoice is accepted.

To proceed we need: your preferred pattern from above, confirmed PO header field mapping (I looked at Healthline_PO_template_v2.pdf), and whether the minimum invoice threshold is negotiable for milestone-based invoices.

Attaching our checklist and a sample pricing slab scenarios file (pricing-slab-scenario.xlsx) for the discount math. If you want, Marissa and Vanessa can review discount tiering and packaging next.

Proposed next step: 30-min call tomorrow to lock on the lane and draft the contract language. I can also pull finance to confirm the acceptance of the PO header fields into our billing system.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: Procurement requirements / pricing lanes proposal

Thanks for the ping. Finance and I modeled two compromise structures in pricing-slab-scenario.xlsx (attached earlier):

A — Prepay credit lane (preferred):
- 3-month minimum prepaid credit (invoice at signing)
- 8% discount on invoiceable consumption drawn from the credit; remaining consumption billed monthly against credit; consolidated statement provided monthly
- If credit exhausted, subsequent usage invoiced net60
- We will accept PO header fields as provided; ERP mapping requires a one-time mapping task (our billing team will handle)

B — Hybrid split:
- 30% up-front, 70% net60; milestone invoices allowed at any point but must meet $1k minimum (unless preauth provided)
- Discount slabs kick in at annual committed ARR thresholds (examples in spreadsheet)

Operational notes:
- Preauth flow: Redwood will create a preauth reference ID when procurement confirms the PO-ack; we can surface that ID on any early invoice to satisfy your AP rules.
- Minimum invoice exception: we can make exceptions for milestone invoices if procurement sends an explicit preapproval (email or DocuSign reference).

My recommendation: offer option A to Healthline — it preserves their desire for a discounted prepaid lane and gives Redwood predictability. Option B is a fallback if they cannot prepay.

Karthik — if you agree, I'll draft a short addendum clause and the invoice routing instructions for the ERP team.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Revenue Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
